subject: SDK Bridge & Cutover Coordination — BlueHarbor integration
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@blueharbor.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: eng-team@blueharbor.com
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: New integration — next steps and cutover window

Vanessa, thanks for the quick sync earlier. As discussed on the call, we want to keep the cutover tight (low-risk, minimal downtime) and make sure the SDK migration doesn't impact token quota unexpectedly. A few items we need from Redwood to finalize our runbook: 

- Recommended SDK package (language + version) for production use.
- A sample endpoint migration script and rollback steps.
- Guidance on per-client rate limits and backoff windows (we currently throttle at 120 reqs/min per API key).
- Any pre-cutover telemetry checks we should run in staging.

I'll put our engineering leads on the thread: eng-team@blueharbor.com. Proposed cutover window: Friday 2027-05-07 02:00–03:30 UTC. Can Redwood support a canary ramp during that hour?

Thanks,
Alex
Lead Integrations, BlueHarbor
[Attachment: blueharbor-current-rates.csv (CSV, 12KB)]

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@blueharbor.com>
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, eng-team@blueharbor.com
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 12:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: New integration — next steps and cutover window

Alex — thanks, this is great context. Looping in Vivek (runtime/inference) and Grace (CSM-implementation) to scope the technical plan. Initial responses inline below, and I attached a concise runbook (blueharbor-integration-plan.pdf) that contains the migration checklist and sample scripts.

High-level answers:
- SDK: we recommend the Redwood client 1.x series for JVM (artifact: com.redwood:client:1.4.2) or 0.9+ for node (npm @redwood-ai/sdk@0.9.1) for stable production builds.
- Canary: yes — we can route a percent of traffic to a canary model variant and autoscale during the window.
- Rate limits: Redwood enforces per-key rate limits with token-bucket smoothing. We suggest initial client-side backoff: 500ms base, exponential jitter to 8s, with 429 handling mapped to a 1.5x base backoff for the first 3 retries.
- Pre-cutover checks: KV cache hit rate > 60% in staging, percentile p95 latency < 220ms for your request shape, and no 5xx regressions.

Action items:
1) Vivek to share endpoint migration script and a short Node/Python sample.
2) BlueHarbor to share staging traffic replay for Thursday run.
3) Agree rollback thresholds and alerting (we'll provide Prometheus alert names).

Vanessa Ortiz
CSM — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | +1 415-555-0187
[Attachment: blueharbor-integration-plan.pdf (PDF, 82KB)]

Thanks Vivek — the samples look good. A couple of engineering questions from our side after review: 

1) We use connection pools in our Node service; any specific keep-alive or max-concurrency recommendations for the /v2/stream endpoint?
2) For the canary variant header approach, will downstream logs preserve original client_id so we can correlate?

Also confirming the dry run time — Thursday 2027-04-29 17:00 UTC works for our infra lead, Kara. We'll forward our staging replay by Wednesday EOD.

Alex
Alex Turner | BlueHarbor Payments

From: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@blueharbor.com>, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: eng-team@blueharbor.com
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 20:02:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: New integration — next steps and cutover window

Alex — quick answers for your infra questions, added here so Kara has what she needs for the dry run: 

1) Connections & concurrency: use keep-alive with a pool of ~50 connections per instance for steady state. For the canary ramp, we recommend increasing pool to 80 during the 30m windows then scale down. Redwood supports HTTP/2 multiplexing on the /v2/stream endpoint — that'll reduce connection counts.

2) Correlation: yes — when you pass client_id in the X-Client-Id header we'll preserve it in request logs and expose the ID in the trace span (trace_id -> user_client_id mapping). We'll share a short runbook of the trace fields you can query in Console.

Prep checklist for dry run (Thursday):
- BlueHarbor: push staging replay to the shared location and confirm file size.
- BlueHarbor: provide an on-call Slack contact for the hour.
- Redwood: we'll share temporary canary keys and Prometheus alert names (redwood.cb.p95.latency, redwood.cb.5xx.rate).

Looking forward to the dry run — I'll post the Console links after we provision the canary.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Implementation Lead, Customer Success
